questions.question: School zone speed limits are always 25 mph.

options.text: True
False

questions.correctAnswerText: False
questions.explanation: In Nevada, school zone speed limits are either 15 mph or 25 mph. These limits apply on school days from 30 minutes before school starts to 30 minutes after school ends, unless a different speed is posted.

questions.question: When parking uphill next to a curb, set the parking brake and:

options.text: Keep the rear tires against the curb.
Keep the front tires straight ahead.
Turn your steering wheel away from the curb.
Turn your steering wheel toward the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your steering wheel away from the curb.
questions.explanation: When parking uphill next to a curb, set your parking brake and turn your steering wheel away from the curb. If your vehicle rolls, it will roll into the curb and stop.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Your current roadway ends ahead.
You must bear either right or left.
A four-way intersection is ahead.
A road joins from the right.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must bear either right or left.
questions.explanation: This sign shows a Y intersection ahead. You must choose to go either right or left.

questions.question: What does a single dashed white line separating traffic mean?

options.text: Drivers may pass, even if it could be dangerous.
Lanes move in opposite directions.
Drivers may not pass.
Drivers may pass if it is safe to do so.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drivers may pass if it is safe to do so.
questions.explanation: White lines separate lanes moving in the same direction. A dashed white line can be crossed to pass or change lanes if it is safe.

questions.question: When using a roundabout, drivers should:

options.text: Yield to traffic already in the roundabout.
Yield to entering traffic.
Drive in a clockwise direction.
Stop in the middle of the roundabout.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield to traffic already in the roundabout.
questions.explanation: A roundabout is a circular intersection with traffic flowing counterclockwise around a center island. When entering, yield to traffic already in the roundabout. Follow the circle to the right until you reach your exit.

questions.question: When driving on slippery roads:

options.text: Always drive at the maximum speed limit.
Use cruise control to maintain a steady speed.
Reduce your following distance.
Do not make any sudden changes in speed or direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not make any sudden changes in speed or direction.
questions.explanation: On slippery roads, avoid sudden changes in speed or direction. Slow down and do not use cruise control.

questions.question: What does a single dashed yellow line separating traffic mean?

options.text: Drivers may pass if it is safe to do so.
Both lanes travel in the same direction.
Drivers may not pass.
Drivers may pass, even if it could be dangerous.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drivers may pass if it is safe to do so.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions. A single dashed yellow line means both directions can pass if safe. Do not pass if oncoming traffic is near.

questions.question: You are approaching an intersection when the traffic light changes from green to solid yellow. You should:

options.text: Consider it the same as a caution sign and continue through the intersection.
Stop immediately.
Stop before entering the intersection, unless you are too close to stop safely.
Speed up to get through the intersection before the red light appears.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop before entering the intersection, unless you are too close to stop safely.
questions.explanation: When the light turns yellow, slow down and stop before entering the intersection if you can do so safely. If you are too close to stop, drive through carefully.

questions.question: If you need to stop quickly and your vehicle does not have Anti-Lock Brakes (ABS), you should:

options.text: Hold down the brake pedal.
Firmly pump your brakes.
Lightly tap the brakes.
Release the brake pedal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Firmly pump your brakes.
questions.explanation: Pumping the brakes is the best emergency stop method. Your car stops quickly and you can still steer.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Intersection.
Road curve.
Right turn.
Lane change.

questions.correctAnswerText: Intersection.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that an intersection with a crossing road is ahead.

questions.question: You hear a siren but cannot see the emergency vehicle yet. What should you do?

options.text: Keep driving until you see the vehicle.
Pull to the curb and look to see if the vehicle is on your street.
Slow down, but don't stop until you see it.
Speed up and turn at the next intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull to the curb and look to see if the vehicle is on your street.
questions.explanation: When you hear a siren but cannot see the emergency vehicle, safely pull over to the right side of the road and stop. Wait until you are sure the vehicle is not coming toward you.

questions.question: What does a "No standing" sign mean?

options.text: You can never stop your vehicle there.
You can park there if the driver stays in the vehicle.
You can stop briefly to pick up or drop off passengers.
You can stop to load or unload cargo.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can stop briefly to pick up or drop off passengers.
questions.explanation: A "No standing" sign means you can only stop for a short time to pick up or drop off passengers.

questions.question: Your vehicle is blocking traffic after an accident. What should you do?

options.text: Move your vehicle off the road if possible.
Do not move your vehicle under any circumstances.
Wait for police to arrive before moving your vehicle.
None of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move your vehicle off the road if possible.
questions.explanation: After a minor accident, move your vehicle off the road if you can. Do not leave the scene without identifying yourself and offering help.

questions.question: What does a solid yellow arrow mean in a traffic signal?

options.text: It is never used as a traffic signal.
It means the same thing as a yellow traffic light.
It means drivers can turn in the direction of the arrow.
It means a green arrow is about to appear.

questions.correctAnswerText: It means the same thing as a yellow traffic light.
questions.explanation: A solid yellow arrow has the same meaning as a regular yellow traffic light. Slow down and prepare to stop when you see it.

questions.question: What is the safest way to back up your vehicle?

options.text: Honk your horn right before putting the car in reverse.
Check behind the vehicle before you sit in the driver's seat.
Use your rearview mirrors to see what is behind you.
Turn up the radio before backing up to alert people nearby.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check behind the vehicle before you sit in the driver's seat.
questions.explanation: Backing up is risky because it is hard to see behind your vehicle. Before you get in to back up, walk to the back and check for children and small objects.

questions.question: How do you check your blind spots when changing lanes?

options.text: Use the inside rearview mirror.
Use the outside rearview mirror.
Use both rearview mirrors.
Turn your head and look over your shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head and look over your shoulder.
questions.explanation: Turn your head to check your blind spots before every lane change.

questions.question: What should drivers do when driving in bad weather?

options.text: Speed up to reach their destination faster.
Drive closer to the car ahead.
Stay farther away from the car ahead.
None of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay farther away from the car ahead.
questions.explanation: On wet roads, increase the distance between your vehicle and the car ahead of you.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Roundabout ahead.
No passing zone.
Left turn yield on green.
Traffic signal ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic signal ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a traffic signal is coming. Slow down and be ready to stop.

questions.question: When driving to a place you don't know, what should you do?

options.text: Follow road signs to find your way.
Plan your trip before you start.
You only need to know where your destination is generally.
Always take the most direct route.

questions.correctAnswerText: Plan your trip before you start.
questions.explanation: Plan your trip in advance when driving to an unfamiliar area. Check your destination on a map before you leave.

questions.question: How can you help prevent crashes?

options.text: Communicate with other road users.
Ignore what other drivers are doing.
Drive only on side streets and back roads.
Avoid driving during rush hour.

questions.correctAnswerText: Communicate with other road users.
questions.explanation: Crashes happen when drivers do something unexpected. Communicate with other drivers, cyclists, and pedestrians by signaling when you slow down, stop, or turn. Use your emergency lights or horn when needed.

questions.question: If a car is coming toward you with blinding headlights, what should you do?

options.text: Turn on your bright lights until the other driver dims theirs.
Flash your lights on and off to warn the other driver.
Dim your lights and then speed up to pass quickly.
Look toward the right side of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look toward the right side of the road.
questions.explanation: If a car is coming toward you with high beams on, look away from the headlights. Look toward the right side of the road until the car passes. This keeps you from being blinded.

questions.question: What is the most common cause of traffic crashes?

options.text: New drivers
Human error
Bad weather
Bad roads

questions.correctAnswerText: Human error
questions.explanation: Crashes often happen when drivers do not see another vehicle or when a driver does something unexpected. Communicate with other drivers to help prevent crashes.

questions.question: What should you always do when approaching a roundabout?

options.text: Speed up.
Keep the same speed.
Stop completely.
Slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: When approaching a roundabout, slow down. A roundabout is designed for low-speed driving.

questions.question: What does a steady green arrow on a traffic signal mean?

options.text: Merge into the lane that the arrow points to.
Slow down and stop if it is safe.
You may turn in the direction of the arrow after letting other vehicles and pedestrians pass.
You may drive straight through the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may turn in the direction of the arrow after letting other vehicles and pedestrians pass.
questions.explanation: A green arrow means you may turn in that direction. You must be in the correct lane. Always let vehicles and pedestrians already in the intersection go first.

questions.question: Can drivers pass on a two-lane road with a single solid yellow line on their side of the center?

options.text: True
False

questions.correctAnswerText: False
questions.explanation: You may pass only when the broken yellow line is on your side of the road. A solid yellow line means you cannot pass.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Turn right after stopping completely.
No right turns allowed.
Left turns are allowed.
None of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: No right turns allowed.
questions.explanation: This is a regulation sign. It shows rules that drivers must follow. Right turns are not allowed where this sign is posted.

questions.question: What is used on some highways to direct drivers into the proper lanes for turning?

options.text: Flashing red lights
Flashing yellow lights
White lines on the side of the road
White arrows in the middle of the lanes

questions.correctAnswerText: White arrows in the middle of the lanes
questions.explanation: White arrows on the road show which lanes to use for turning or going straight.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Hunting area.
State park.
Deer may cross the road here.
Wildlife preserve.

questions.correctAnswerText: Deer may cross the road here.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that deer cross the road in this area. Slow down, stay alert, and be ready to stop.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: No right turns.
Keep to the right.
No U-turns.
The left lane must turn left.

questions.correctAnswerText: No right turns.
questions.explanation: This regulation sign shows rules drivers must follow. It means right turns are not allowed.

questions.question: What is the leading cause of traffic accidents in Nevada?

options.text: Speeding.
Not yielding the right-of-way.
Following too closely.
Driving under the influence.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not yielding the right-of-way.
questions.explanation: Not yielding the right-of-way is the leading cause of traffic accidents in Nevada. Learn Nevada's right-of-way rules and be ready to give up your right-of-way to prevent accidents.
